plates.side_label: VON FRISCH (1946): STRAIGHT UP = SUN ANGLE & ~1 S WAGGLE ≈ 1 KM DISTANCE
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Honeybee Waggle Dance Sun-to-Gravity Vector Code, Polarized-Light Compass & 1989 Robot Bee Recruitment chart from Karl von Frisch (1914 Zool. Jahrb., 1946 Experientia 2: 397–405 & 1949 Experientia 5: 142–148), Martin Lindauer (1955 Z. vergl. Physiol. 37: 263–324), and Axel Michelsen, Wolfgang Kirchner & Martin Lindauer (1989 Naturwissenschaften 76: 277–280) shows 1) Outside: angle alpha between the Sun and the food source; 2) Inside on the vertical dark comb: waggle run angled at that exact angle alpha relative to straight up (gravity), where ~1 second of waggling ≈ 1 km distance; and 3) Michelsen's 1989 brass-and-wax robot bee vibrating at 280 Hz recruiting real bees to targets 250–1,000 m away.

teach_overlay.label: 1946 KARL VON FRISCH (EXPERIENTIA 2: 397): SUN-TO-GRAVITY WAGGLE ANGLE & ~1 S ≈ 1,000 M DISTANCE CURVE
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Karl von Frisch (1946 Experientia 2: 397–405) waggle dance angle (0° straight up = toward Sun; 60° right of vertical = 60° right of Sun; 180° straight down = away from Sun) & waggle-run duration vs distance curve (~1 second waggle run ≈ 1,000 metres flight distance) on period paper
teach_overlay.scale: a honeybee's brain weighs just one milligram — a millionth of a kilogram, smaller than a single sesame seed — yet inside a pitch-black hive she converts the angle of the Sun in the sky into the pull of gravity under her feet with the precision of a compass
who_cards: Karl Ritter von Frisch (1886–1982) — Austrian ethologist and zoologist
